title: RSI: Repair scope and pruning
question: What may a repair change, and what does pruning a skill mean?

origin.title: RSI: Repair scope and pruning

history.reason: Capture an unresolved choice from the agent proposal before the owner first pass; alignment only.

proposal.readback:
**Question:** What may a repair change, and what does pruning a skill mean?

**Recommended answer:** Diagnose the owning cause first. Simplify or remove instructions only when evidence supports it, preserving requirements and provenance. Allow shared-skill and produced-Workbench repairs within their assigned scope; route unrelated product defects and third-party changes to their owners.

**Why:** I assumed the smallest repair was preferred, but pruning must not become automatic shortening or uncontrolled changes to every project.

**Intended impact:** Defines repair boundaries and protects useful behavior while reducing avoidable complexity.

events.note: "What does a pruning skill mean" is a scary question. Its our pruning skill. The one I had us create to replace the duplicated process in author skill and writing for agents. This is how we create skills. We use '/author-skill, add it everything we need to make it work, prune it using the '/prune skill we made, and then run it through the regression audit. each run gets an alignment score on the rubric, and the whole skill gets a fitness level grade between broken and excellent and an alignment score based on those 3 runs. We log the result for the RSI loop, its failures, etc. And then run it again where we author skill, prune and run it through the regression audit until we get a stable or excellent skill that passes the alignment score, and doesn't fail any more of the failures we have recorded (regressed)
